title: Next-generation ensemble projections reveal higher climate risks for marine ecosystems
field: Climate change impacts on marine ecosystems
problem: Projections of climate change impacts on marine ecosystems using previous-generation CMIP5 models may underestimate risks, as they do not incorporate the updated oceanographic drivers and increased climate sensitivity of the newer CMIP6 Earth system models.
method: This study applies an enhanced suite of global marine ecosystem models, forced by new-generation CMIP6 Earth system model outputs, to project climate change impacts on ocean ecosystems and compares these results with previous CMIP5-forced projections to assess future climate risks.
task: The task is to project climate change impacts on marine ecosystems by forcing an enhanced suite of ecosystem models with new-generation CMIP6 outputs and comparing the results to projections forced by the previous CMIP5 generation.
innovation: This paper presents new ensemble projections using CMIP6 climate models which reveal a greater decline in global marine animal biomass and thus higher climate risks for marine ecosystems compared to previous projections based on CMIP5 models.

For the Fish-MIP simulation round here, to enable the best possible comparison between CMIP5 and CMIP6, we utilized the same two ESMs: GFDL-ESM2M51,52 and IPSL-CM5A-LR53 for CMIP5 and the equivalent new generations for CMIP6, GFDL-ESM4.154–56 and IPSL-CM6A-LR57–59.

Fig. 1 | Projected mean global change in oceanographic properties from IPSL and GFDL ESMs. a–h, Rows depict SST (a,b), NPP (c,d), phytoplankton carbon (e,f) and zooplankton carbon (g,h) for GFDL and IPSL CMIP5 and CMIP6 under strong-mitigation (blue) and high-emissions (red) scenarios. Historical values (1970–2005 for CMIP5; 1970–2014 for CMIP6) are shown in black, and projections (2006–2099 for CMIP5; 2015–2099 for CMIP6) are coloured. All values are normalized relative to the period 1990–1999. Vertical grey shaded area indicates reference decade, and vertical grey line indicates first year of projection (subsequent to historical period). RCP, representative concentration pathway.

CMIP6 models exhibit increased climate sensitivity (the equilibrium response of mean surface air temperature to a doubling of atmospheric CO2) over CMIP519, resulting in generally stronger marine ecosystem forcings (for example, ocean warming) under the high-emissions scenario, although with more variation in terms of impacts on net primary productivity (NPP)17,20.
